newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee slips in AM after spectacular rally.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee slips in AM after spectacular rally.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures were lower across the board by Friday midsession in a reversal to Thursday's spectacular rally to 20-month-highs.
Traders said the retracement, accelerated by scale-up producer selling, was not unexpected as the market was well overbought.
"Some robusta producers who have been backing off before now decided that it is time to sell," said one trader.
By the morning close, benchmark July was $59 lower at $2,541 a tonne after gapping $50 higher at the open. Its intraday high was $2,660 and just below Thursday's peak of $2,670.
Most other months were headed lower.
Thursday's frenzied roaster-led buying lifted July by almost 20 percent at one stage.

The rally, which saw prices rising by almost 14 percent in the morning alone, gathered steam in the afternoon as New York's July arabica coffee futures whizzed past the $3 a lb mark, not seen for 20 years.
Traders said a failure by New York's September to close above 274 cents, the 1994 high, could set the contract back towards the 240 area.
But despite this, the current bullish scenario has not changed and traders said the market could still push higher as the Brazilian winter approaches.
Private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday temperatures in Brazil's coffee belt would be below normal through Sunday but no damanging cold was expected.
